title: Letter informing Southwest Power Pool, Inc. that the 02/10/2026 filing is deficient and requesting additional information to be filed within 30 days to assist in processing its proposed revisions to its Open Access Transmission Tariff etc., ER26-1323.

documents.name: ER26-1323-000 Deficiency Letter.docx
documents.text:
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION
WASHINGTON, DC  20426

OFFICE OF ENERGY MARKET REGULATION

								In Reply Refer To:
				Southwest Power Pool, Inc. 
Docket No. ER26-1323-000
	
March 30, 2026

Southwest Power Pool, Inc.
201 Worthen Drive
Little Rock, AR  72223-4936

Attention:  Emon O. Mahony

Reference:  Deficiency Letter

Dear Mr. Mahony:

On February 10, 2026, Southwest Power Pool, Inc. (SPP) filed proposed revisions to its Open Access Transmission Tariff (Tariff) to add a new type of transmission service, Conditional High Impact Large Load Service (CHILLS), to serve High Impact Large Loads (HILLs).  As part of its filing, SPP proposes to add a new Part VII (Conditional High Impact Large Load Transmission Service) and Schedule 15 (Conditional High Impact Large Load Transmission Service) to its Tariff to implement CHILLS.  In addition, SPP proposes revisions to Attachment BA (High Impact Large Loads), Attachment AE (Integrated Marketplace), Attachment AQ (Delivery Point Assessment Process), and Attachment AX (Provisional Load Process) in its Tariff to implement CHILLS.  SPP also proposes to add a new study process to its Tariff, contained in Attachment BC (High Impact Large Load Delivery Point Initial Assessment), for HILLs that bring their own generating resources to provide CHILLS.  Additionally, SPP proposes to add a new pro forma CHILLS Service Agreement (CHILLSA) and a new pro forma CHILLS Operating Agreement to its Tariff.  SPP states that the pro forma CHILLSA and the pro forma CHILLS Operating Agreement are modeled on its existing pro forma transmission service agreements.  
SPP explains that its CHILLS proposal will allow HILLs to receive energy on a long-term, non-firm basis in instances where transmission service is unavailable due to the lack of existing designated generating resources or network upgrades necessary to provide firm transmission service.  SPP explains that CHILLS is an “as available” transmission service that will utilize the transmission system’s excess transfer capability that is not needed to serve native load or other customers.  SPP states that CHILLS will have equal priority to monthly non-firm point-to-point transmission service.  In addition, SPP explains that CHILLS requires supporting generation and that SPP will curtail CHILLS when the supporting generating resource is not available.  SPP states that CHILLS is also subject to curtailment and interruption on a non-discriminatory basis in the event the transmission system is constrained or under emergency or other unforeseen conditions.  
Please be advised that the submittal is deficient and that additional information is necessary to process the filing.  Please provide the information requested below and provide citations to any relevant, proposed Tariff and business practice manual provisions that support your answers to this letter.
SPP proposes three avenues by which a transmission customer can obtain CHILLS:  Attachments AQ, AX, and BC.  Please explain when an eligible customer must submit a CHILLS application relative to when it must submit a request for a delivery point addition or modification to be studied under Attachments AQ, AX, or BC and whether additional Tariff revisions are needed to clarify this timeframe.   

In proposed Part VII, section 47.1, SPP proposes that, after an eligible customer submits an application for CHILLS, SPP will acknowledge receipt of the application.  The proposed Tariff language further provides that “[t]he acknowledgment must include a date by which a response, including a CHILLSA, will be sent to the Eligible Customer.”  Additionally, proposed Part VII, section 47.2 (Time Requirements) of the Tariff provides that the evaluation of CHILLS requests will follow the timing requirements of Attachment P (Transmission Service Timing Requests).  SPP’s proposed revisions to Attachment P provide that SPP will respond to the application “[a]t the Completion of Studies Outlined in Attachments AQ, AX, BA, and/or BC.”  Finally, proposed Part VII, section 44.3 (Service Agreements) of the Tariff states that SPP will provide a CHILLSA to an eligible customer when the customer first submits a completed CHILLS application.  Please explain when SPP must tender a CHILLSA relative to when an eligible customer submits a valid CHILLS application and whether additional Tariff revisions are needed to clarify this timeframe.  

SPP proposes that Attachment BC apply “when it becomes necessary or desirable to establish a HILL delivery point or make changes in facilities at a HILL delivery point and the Network Customer or Transmission Customer does not have enough existing designated resources or planned designated resources to serve the increased load plus losses.”  To be studied under the proposed Attachment BC, a transmission customer must have sufficient generation capacity to support the HILL that are not designated or planned designated resources.  

In section 1.0 of Attachment BC, SPP proposes to require a network customer or transmission customer to submit a request for a HILL Delivery Point Limitations Assessment (HDPLA).  In relevant part, SPP proposes:

The Network Customer or Transmission Customer will submit a request for a HILL Delivery Point Limitations Assessment (“HDPLA”) in writing to (a) the Transmission Provider and the Host Transmission Owner as specified in Section 20 of the Network Operating Agreement or (b) the Transmission Provider as specified in Section 8 of the Point-To-Point Transmission Service Agreement, as applicable.
Please explain whether a transmission customer requesting to establish or modify a HILL delivery point must have an existing NOA or point-to-point transmission service agreement and, if not, please explain how such a customer would submit a HDPLA request under section 1.0 of Attachment BC. 
In section 2.2 (Transmission System Study) of Attachment BC (High Impact Large Load Delivery Point Initial Assessment), SPP proposes that: “Upon receipt of the Request for a HDPLA, Transmission Provider will perform an assessment of the impact of the requested delivery point configuration change on the Transmission System . . . .”  Later in section 2.2, SPP proposes that a HILL without designated resources or planned designated resources sufficient to cover the HILL will be subject to the HDPLA “described below.”  Proposed section 2.2 proceeds to describe the HDPLA as assessing the impacts to the transmission system “caused by requested HILL delivery point additions or modifications.”  SPP further proposes that it will send a study report to the transmission customer and the host transmission owner.  Please clarify whether the “assessment” described in section 2.2 of Attachment BC is the HDPLA.  If not, please explain how that “assessment” and the HDPLA differ and explain whether SPP issues a separate study report for the HDPLA. 

In section 2.2 of Attachment BC, SPP proposes:
The HDPLA study results do not establish a HILL delivery point for load that cannot be served by currently planned generation and/or Designated Resources until after the Transmission Customer or Network Customer executes a Service Agreement pursuant to Attachment AQ, Attachment AX, or Attachment BA of the Tariff, for such load.
Please explain how and why a transmission customer proceeding through the Attachment BC study process would execute a service agreement under Attachment AQ or Attachment AX to establish a HILL delivery point for load that cannot be served by currently planned generation and/or designated resources.  In your response, please explain why the CHILLSA, the service agreement pursuant to Attachment BA, would not be the appropriate service agreement to establish a HILL delivery point for such load. 

The Commission’s pro forma Open Access Transmission Tariff includes provisions governing situations in which a transmission customer requests that a transmission service agreement be filed with the Commission unexecuted.  Similarly, SPP’s existing Tariff provides such processes for its existing transmission services.  SPP states that it has substantially modeled CHILLS on existing transmission services because CHILLS shares similarities with such services.  Please explain whether the proposed Tariff revisions allow eligible customers to request that the transmission provider file an unexecuted CHILLSA or unexecuted CHILLS Operating Agreement with the Commission and, if not, why the absence of such provisions is just and reasonable and not unduly discriminatory or preferential.

Please explain how and under what conditions SPP will shed or curtail CHILLS, given that SPP equates CHILLS’s priority to non-firm point-to-point transmission service.  In your response, please explain whether transmission loading relief procedures pursuant to Attachment R in the Tariff will apply to CHILLS curtailments, similar to non-firm point-to-point transmission service.  If so, please state the priority level that would be assigned to CHILLS.  Please also explain whether SPP will curtail CHILLS for economic reasons, similar to non-firm point-to-point transmission service.  

In sections 5.1.2 (Day-Ahead Market Execution), 5.2.2 (Day-Ahead Reliability Unit Commitment Execution), and 6.1.2 (Intra-Day Reliability Unit Commitment Execution) of Attachment AE, SPP proposes revisions to various provisions governing manual resource commitments to include reductions of CHILLS.  SPP proposes that it will manually commit or reduce a CHILL or CHILLS.  SPP’s existing Tariff language provides that manual commitments will be verified by the market monitor (i.e., SPP MMU) though the process described in section 6.1.2.1 (Determination of Non-Discriminatory Manual Resource Selection).  Please explain whether CHILL and CHILLS reductions, as provided for in Attachment AE, will be monitored for non-discriminatory treatment by the SPP MMU.  If not, please explain why not.  If so, please explain how the Tariff provides for this.  

SPP proposes that the CHILLS commencement date can be extended for up to one year if requested by the transmission customer and no later than 60 days before the commencement of CHILLS, but that such an extension will require a non-refundable annual reservation fee.  SPP further proposes that it will release a transmission customer’s CHILLS Reserved Capacity if another transmission customer submits a completed application during the extension period that can only be satisfied by releasing part or all of the original transmission customer’s CHILLS Reserved Capacity, unless the original transmission customer pays “the CHILLS transmission rate for its CHILLS Reserved Capacity.”  Please explain whether the required payment (i.e., “the CHILLS transmission rate for its CHILLS Reserved Capacity”) for an original transmission customer to keep its CHILLS Reserved Capacity during an extension period, when such CHILLS Reserved Capacity is needed to satisfy the request of a subsequent CHILLS applicant, is the CHILLS transmission rate for the entire term of the transmission customer’s CHILLS, the extension period, or some other term. 

SPP proposes a new Schedule 15 to provide the rates for CHILLS.  SPP states that it modeled the rates for CHILLS on the existing rates for non-firm point-to-point transmission service, due to various similarities in the nature of both services, and adopts Schedule 11 (Base Plan Zonal Charge) charges similar to both point-to-point transmission service and NITS.  However, SPP’s proposed Schedule 15 does not include the subregional charge contained in Schedule 11 in the rates for CHILLS.  Please explain why SPP does not propose to include the subregional charge contained in Schedule 11 in the rates charged for CHILLS under proposed Schedule 15. 

SPP further proposes that, in the event a CHILLS customer exceeds its CHILLS Reserved Capacity amount at any point of delivery, the CHILLS customer must pay (in addition to the charges for the CHILLS capacity used) a penalty charge equal to:  100% of the non-firm point-to-point transmission service charges under Schedules 8 (Non-Firm Point-To-Point Transmission Service) and Schedule 11 for the period when the additional service was used during the month for the amount in excess of such capacity reservation.  SPP proposes to compensate transmission owners for the service by allocating penalty revenues to them, similar to its existing practices for distributing penalties collected for overuse of non-firm point-to-point transmission service.  However, SPP’s proposed compensation to transmission owners for overuse of CHILLS does not include the subregional charge under Schedule 11.  Specifically, this proposed compensation to transmission owners will consist of 100% of the:  (1) CHILLS charge; (2) base plan zonal charge; and (3) region-wide charge for the period for which the transmission owners have provided service.  Please explain why SPP does not propose to include the subregional charge contained in Schedule 11 in the proposed penalty charged to a CHILLS customer that exceeds its CHILLS Reserved Capacity. 

SPP states that when network load and a CHILL are located at the same point of delivery with behind-the-meter generation, the network load must be adjusted for any excess hourly generation above the CHILLS Reserved Capacity.  SPP states that it is necessary to adjust the network load by adding the amount of excess hourly generation to ensure all generation and load amounts are properly addressed through settlement and to prevent any netting of loads reported for NITS.  The SPP MMU contends that SPP’s formula for determining network load when CHILLS load and behind-the-meter generation are at the same delivery point is incorrect, and suggests that excess generation should simply be the generation above the actual CHILLS load, rather than the CHILLS Reserved Capacity.  In its answer, SPP reiterates its use of CHILLS Reserved Capacity, but states that the exact nature of the adjustment can vary with the metering configuration and that the exact formula need not be in the Tariff.  

Please explain why SPP proposes to calculate the excess hourly generation of behind-the-meter generation in this arrangement based on the CHILLS Reserved Capacity rather than the actual CHILLS load.  

Please explain how the adjustments can vary with the metering configuration.  In your response, please provide examples of the adjustment with at least two different metering configurations. 

In section 17.0 of the CHILLSA, SPP proposes the following:
The actual hourly CHILLS load and any firm load, by delivery point, internal generation site, and point where power may flow to or from the Transmission Customer or Network Customer, with separate readings for each direction of flow, must be provided.
Please explain whether this proposed language establishes a metering requirement for network load in order to provide the “firm load” amounts.  If the proposed language does establish such a requirement, please explain why SPP proposes to establish such a requirement in a CHILLSA to which the network load is not a party. 

The SPP MMU also suggests that SPP should reassess allowing Load Responsible Entities (LRE) to use the same capacity to cover a CHILL that is used to meet their resource adequacy requirement.  Please explain whether the same capacity used to cover a CHILL is allowed to be used in an LRE’s workbook to meet an LRE’s resource adequacy requirement.  In your response, please also explain whether CHILLs are included in forecasts of Net Peak Demand used to determine an LRE’s resource adequacy requirement. 

In SPP’s proposed Schedule 15, there are two sections with the same section numbering:  “4. Discounts” and “4. Real Power Losses.”  Please explain why SPP proposes to assign two different sections the same section number.

Proposed section 2.22.2 (Resources Supporting a HILL or CHILL) of Attachment AE states that it applies to “Resources Supporting a HILL or a CHILL.”  In proposed section 2.22.2(3) of Attachment AE, SPP proposes “Behind-The-Meter Generation supporting a HILL and registered in the Integrated Marketplace . . . .”  Please explain whether proposed section 2.22.2(3) also applies to a CHILL.  If not, please explain why such provision is not applicable to a CHILL. 
This letter is issued pursuant to 18 C.F.R. § 375.307 (2025) and is interlocutory.  This letter is not subject to rehearing pursuant to 18 C.F.R. § 385.713 (2025).  A response to this letter must be filed with the Secretary of the Commission within 30 days of the date of this letter by making a deficiency filing in accordance with the Commission’s electronic tariff requirements.  For your response, please use Type of Filing Code 180, Deficiency Filing.  The information requested in this letter will constitute an amendment to your filing, and a new filing date will be established.  A notice will be issued upon receipt of your filing.
Failure to respond to this letter within the time period specified may result in a further order rejecting your filing.
Issued by:  Natalie Y. Tingle-Stewart, Director, Division of Electric Power Regulation – Central
